title: AI Engineer (mid to senior, remote, LatAm)

questionnaire.text: Tell us about an LLM feature you shipped to production. What did it do, who used it, and what was your part?
How did you know its output was good enough? Describe how you measured quality.
What is the hardest AI-related problem you have solved, and how?
When do you choose plain code, an agent, or retrieval? Give one real example of a deliberate choice.
Where are you based, what is your hourly rate in USD, how do you rate your English from 1 to 10, and how many hours a day can you overlap with US Eastern time?

criteria.text: Has shipped LLM features to production
evidence_signals: names a specific system or feature they built
says who used it or at what volume
describes their own part, not only the team's

criteria.text: Measures output quality (evals, test sets, agreement with humans)
evidence_signals: mentions a test set, labeled examples or a golden set
names a metric and how it changed
compares model output with human reviewers

criteria.text: Chooses between code, agents and retrieval on purpose
evidence_signals: gives a real example of keeping something in plain code, using retrieval, or using an agent instead of the model
the reason is stated, or evident from the split itself (for example: exact values never pass through the model)

criteria.text: Has run or compared open-weight language models
evidence_signals: names an open-weight language model they ran or compared (e.g. Llama, Qwen, Mistral)
reports a result of that comparison (quality, cost or speed)
